state.purpose: Combine the fast-cash action-ticket frontier with effect readback, without adding patch-generation or execution liability. Optimize for highest realized owner hourly earnings reached quickly and for transferable company assets.

priorFindings: Z2 action-ticket factory had fastest time-to-cash (.24) and low owner/domain/customer-risk within the action-ready generation.
Z4 action-ticket + savings receipt had much stronger sellable-asset properties (.37 asset weakness) but slower time-to-cash (.43).
IaC patch generation improved actionability/commoditization somewhat but materially increased setup, liability, support and owner work.
world.designBoundary: No generated code/patches and no execution authority. Differentiate through precise action artifacts plus deterministic readback lineage.

candidates.name: action-ticket-baseline
candidates.claim: For each high-value cloud-cost finding, return a standardized action ticket with exact resource, action, evidence, expected savings, risk notes, validation and rollback steps. Customer executes every action. Up to four annual refreshes can repeat the same workflow.

candidates.name: top3-ticket-plus-receipt
candidates.claim: Return only the top three evidence-backed action tickets by expected annualized savings. Customer marks which ticket IDs it executed. On the next billing export, the factory automatically produces an effect receipt for those IDs: observed spend delta, expected-vs-observed savings, confounders and status. No code generation or execution. Same fixed schema repeats on refresh.

candidates.name: savings-ledger-refresh
candidates.claim: Same top-three ticket workflow as AA2, but every proposal, customer execution status and subsequent effect receipt is appended to a versioned savings ledger. The first paid audit includes one readback. If useful, it converts to a prepaid annual plan with up to four refresh/readback cycles. The ledger becomes the canonical customer-specific history of proposed and realized savings.

candidates.name: unbounded-ticket-ledger
candidates.claim: Produce all detected action tickets, track customer execution and maintain effect receipts/ledger for every action across recurring refreshes. No code generation or execution.

candidates.name: top1-proof-cycle
candidates.claim: For the first paid audit, return only one highest-value, low-risk action ticket and include one automatic post-execution effect receipt. The goal is to prove one savings cycle with minimal setup. Only after that proof does the customer buy a larger three-ticket or annual refresh package using the identical schema.

constraints: No code or patch generation in this generation.
First paid scope must be bounded and file/export based.
Effect receipt uses billing/export readback and exact ticket IDs.
Unsupported or ambiguous findings fail closed rather than require owner research by default.
No full platform before repeated paid demand.
